full_judgment: The petitioner was given a license for import of wire nails under Own IV/H-2/II of the Import Trade Control Schedule. He imported wire nails of BWG No. 18" X 1". On arrival of the goods, respondent No. 1 issued a show .cause notice on 5.8 67 as to why penal action should not be taken against him for contravening section 19 of the Sea Customs Act read with section 3 (3) of the Imports and Exports (Control) Act t XXXIX of 1950) and punishable under clause 8 (b) of section it 7 of the Sea Customs Act. The petitioner denied the charge and stated that the goods imported were wire nails which fall under item No. IVI H-2/11 and as such he had not contravened the provisions of law. The petitioner further desired that he should be heard in person to explain his position. Then on 7.9 67 the Collector of Custom, Chittagong (respondent No. 1) confiscated the goods under section 167 of the Sea Customs Act but gave an option to the petitioner u/s 183 of the said Act to pay a fine of Rs. 27,000/-. He further imposed a penalty of Rs 27,000/- u/s 167(8) (b) of the Sea Customs Act. The respondent noted the contention of the petitioner that the imported wire nails were used in their industry and Observed "but this Customs House does not contest the use of the goods in their industry". The petitioner also filed a certificate from his manufacturer showing that the imported goods were wire nails. However, the petitioner filed an appeal against the order of the respondent No. I to the Central Board of Revenue and the Central Board of Revenue by its order dated 16th August, 1969, after hearing the appellants Counsel, allowed the appeal in part, by setting aside the imposition of the Persona I penalty u/s 167(8)(b) of the Sea Customs Act and reducing the fine in lieu of confiscation of Rs, 13.500.00.
